# Quantum Betti geometric Langlands functor

**Authors:** Ekaterina Bogdanova Address: Harvard University, USA Email address: ebogdanova@math.harvard.edu

## Abstract

We construct the quantum geometric Langlands functor in the Betti setting via Whittaker coefficients. We show that the functor is compatible with the 2-Fourier-Mukai equivalence between sheaves of categories over 2-stacks ${\operatorname{Ge}}_{Z_{G}}$ and ${\operatorname{Ge}}_{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}$ , which classify gerbes on $X$ with respect to the center $Z_{G}$ of $G$ and algebraic fundamental group $\pi_{1}(\check{G})$ of $\check{G}$ .

## 1. Introduction.

The goal of this paper is to construct the functor

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})\xrightarrow{{\mathbb{L}}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{Betti}}}\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G}) $$

between the category of twisted automorphic sheaves with singular support in the global nilpotent cone to the topological factorization homology of $\Rep_{q}(\check{G})$ . The existence of such functor was conjectured in [BZN16] and it is expected to be an equivalence.

At the limit $\kappa\rightarrow\kappa_{\operatorname{crit}}$ we recover the functor ${\mathbb{L}}^{\operatorname{Betti}}$ constructed in [GR24a]. However, our construction uses Whittaker coefficients instead of Hecke action, and thus works in the quantum context as well.

### 1.1. Betti quantum geometric Langlands theory.

The story of geometric Langlands correspondence begin with the following observation. Analogous to the space of automorphic forms, the category of automoprhic sheaves carries a family of commuting Hecke operations given by elements $V\in{\operatorname{Shv}}(\Gra_{G})^{L^{+}G}$ for every point $x\in X$ . Here $\Gra_{G}$ stands for the affine Grassmannian, i.e. the quotient $LG/L^{+}G$ of the loop group of $G$ by the arc group.

#### Theorem 1.1.1.

For every irreducible $\check{G}$ -local system $\sigma$ there exists a unique Hecke eigensheaf with eigenvalue $\sigma$ .

This statement is due to Deligne for $G=\GL_{1}$ , Drinfeld for $G=\GL_{2}$ , Frenkel-Gaitsgory-Vilonen for $G=\GL_{n}$ , and Arinkin, Beraldo, Campbell, Chen, Faergeman, Gaitsgory, Lin, Raskin and Rozenblyum for general $G$ .

#### 1.1.2. Global geometric Langlands conjectures.

Lifting the object-wise statement of Theorem 1.1.1 led Beilinson and Drinfeld to the formulation of the global geometric Langlands correspondence, which says (roughly) that

#### Theorem 1.1.3 ([GR24a], [ABC+24a], [CCF+24], [ABC+24b], [GR24b]).

There exists a canonical equivalence of derived categories

$$ \D(\Bun_{G})\xrightarrow[\cong]{{\mathbb{L}}}\QCoh({\operatorname{LS}}_{\check{G}}), $$

where $\Bun_{G}$ is the moduli stack of $G$ -bundles and ${\operatorname{LS}}_{\check{G}}$ is the stack parameterizing de Rham local systems on $X$ .

The Betti global geometric Langlands correspondence was introduced by Ben-Zvi and Nadler in [BZN16] as a version of Theorem 1.1.3 in the Betti sheaf-theoretic context, which still remembers information of Theorem 1.1.1 and fits into the context of topological field theory (compared to Theorem 1.1.3 which fits into conformal field theory). The Betti Langlands correspondence states (roughly):

#### Theorem 1.1.4.

There exists a canonical equivalence of derived categories

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})\xrightarrow[\cong]{{\mathbb{L}}^{\operatorname{Betti}}}\QCoh({\operatorname{LS}}^{\operatorname{Betti}}_{\check{G}}), $$

where ${\operatorname{LS}}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{Betti}}$ is the stack of Betti $\check{G}$ -local systems. In [GR24a] it is proved that Theorem 1.1.4 is equivalent to the de Rham Langlands correspondence, and thus the proof of Theorem 1.1.3 gives a proof of the Betti version as well.

#### 1.1.5. Quantization of global geometric Langlands conjectures.

However, both the theory of modular/automorphic forms and quantum field theory suggest that there should be a generalization of Theorem 1.1.3 and Theorem 1.1.4. And indeed, both sides of the equivalences ${\mathbb{L}}$ and ${\mathbb{L}}^{\operatorname{Betti}}$ deform over the space of levels for the groups $G$ and $\check{G}$ respectively. A level $\kappa$ for $G$ is by definition a $W$ -invariant bilinear form on the Cartan Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}$ of $\mathfrak{g}$ , whose inverse is a similar kind of datum for $\check{\mathfrak{g}}$ . For a simple reductive group $G$ the space of levels is 1-dimensional. Let us temporarily be in that situation. The main idea of Drinfeld, further studied by Stoyanovsky and Gaitsgory-Lysenko is to consider twisted sheaves/ $D$ -modules.

Let ${\mathcal{L}}_{\det}$ denote the determinant line bundle on $\Bun_{G}$ , i.e., the line bundle whose fiber at a point ${\mathcal{P}}_{G}\in\Bun_{G}$ is $\det R\Gamma(X,\mathfrak{g}_{{\mathcal{P}}_{G}})$ . Let ${\mathcal{L}}_{\det}$ denote the determinant line bundle on $\Bun_{G}$ , i.e., the line bundle whose fiber at a point ${\mathcal{P}}_{G}\in\Bun_{G}$ is $\det R\Gamma(X,\mathfrak{g}_{{\mathcal{P}}_{G}})$ . Then for every $c\in k$ denote by $\D_{c}(\Bun_{G})$ the derived category of D-modules twisted by ${\frac{c-\check{h}}{2\check{h}}}$ -th power of ${\mathcal{L}}_{\det}$ , where $\check{h}$ is the dual Coxeter number of $G$ . Let $r$ be be the maximal multiplicity of arrows in the Dynkin diagram of $G$ . Then the de Rham quantum global geometric Langlands conjecture says

#### Conjecture 1.

There exists a canonical equivalence of derived categories

$$ \D_{c}(\Bun_{G})\xrightarrow[\cong]{{\mathbb{L}}_{c}}\D_{-\frac{1}{rc}}(\Bun_{\check{G}}). $$

At the limit $c\rightarrow 0$ the category $\D_{-\frac{1}{rc}}(\Bun_{\check{G}})$ becomes $\QCoh({\operatorname{LS}}_{G})$ , so Conjecture 1 limits to Theorem 1.1.3. However, note that unlike Theorem 1.1.3, Conjecture 1 is symmetric.

The quantum Betti global geometric Langlands equivalence in the Betti setting was introduced in [BZN16] and states that

#### Conjecture 2.

There exists a canonical equivalence of derived categories

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{c,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})\xrightarrow[\cong]{{\mathbb{L}}_{c}^{\operatorname{Betti}}}\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G}). $$

Here the right-hand side is the derived category of appropriately twisted Betti sheaves with singular support in the global nilpotent cone. Let us explain the left-hand side, which is factorization homology of the category of representations of the quantum group. Note that for $q=1$ we have

$$ \int_{X}\Rep(\check{G})\cong\QCoh({\operatorname{LS}}_{\check{G}}), $$

so in the limit $c\rightarrow 0$ Conjecture 2 recovers Theorem 1.1.4.

#### 1.1.6. Topological factorization homology.

The theory of factorization homology derives from the factorization algebras of Beilinson and Drinfeld ([BD04]), and is a topological version of their theory. Factorization homology with coefficients in $n$ -disk algebras are homology theories for topological manifolds satisfying a generalization of the Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms for ordinary homology; as such, it generalizes ordinary homology in a way that is only defined on $n$ -manifolds and not necessarily on arbitrary topological spaces. Second, these homology theories define topological quantum field theories ([CG17]). An important special case is that of associative algebras where factorization homology over the circle recovers Hochschild homology.

Let us comment on the definition of $\int_{M}A$ for a topological $n$ -manifold $M$ and an ${\mathbb{E}}_{M}$ -algebra $A$ in the sense of [Lur17, 5.4]. We can think of $A$ as a (appropriately twisted) family of ${\mathbb{E}}_{n}$ -algebras $A_{x}$ parameterized by $x\in M$ . In [Lur17, Chapter 5], Lurie proposes a convenient geometric way to encode this data. He defines the topological Ran space ${\operatorname{Ran}}(M)$ as the collection of all nonempty finite subsets of $M$ . Then he defines a cosheaf ${\mathcal{F}}_{A}$ , whose stalk at $S\in{\operatorname{Ran}}(M)$ is $\otimes_{s\in S}A_{s}$ . We can view ${\mathcal{F}}_{A}$ as a constructible cosheaf of ${\operatorname{Ran}}(M)$ , obtained by gluing together locally constant cosheaves along the locally closet subsets of ${\operatorname{Ran}}(M)$ .

We refer to the global sections ${\mathcal{F}}_{A}({\operatorname{Ran}}(M))$ as the topological factorization homology of $M$ with coefficients in $A$ . A collection of striking properties of this construction is formulated and proved in [Lur17, Chapter 5.5].

### 1.2. Main result.

The goal of this paper is to construct the quantum Betti Langlands functor ${\mathbb{L}}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{Betti}}$ of Conjecture 2.

First, let us mention that in the non-quantum case the construction of the functor is given in [GR24a]. Namely, they define the functor

$$ {\mathbb{L}}^{\operatorname{coarse},\operatorname{Betti},L}:\QCoh({\operatorname{LS}}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{Betti}})\rightarrow{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\Nilp}(\Bun_{G}) $$

as follows. Recall that via geometric Satake the Hecke action defines an action of $\Rep(\check{G})$ on ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})$ for every point $x\in X$ . In [NY19] Nadler and Yun showed that this action is locally constant with respect to the point of $X$ , and hence gives a natural action of $\QCoh({\operatorname{LS}}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{Betti}})$ on ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})$ . Then the functor ${\mathbb{L}}^{\operatorname{coarse},\operatorname{Betti},L}$ is given by acting on a certain object

$$ {\operatorname{Poinc}}_{!}^{\operatorname{Vac},\operatorname{glob}}\in{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\Nilp}(\Bun_{G}). $$

Lastly, in [GR24a] it is proved that ${\mathbb{L}}^{\operatorname{coarse},\operatorname{Betti},L}$ admits a right adjoint ${\mathbb{L}}^{\operatorname{coarse},\operatorname{Betti}}$ .

However, one of the main defects of the quantum setting is that the Hecke action is more degenerate: for instance, for irrational $c$ the category ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{c}(\Gra_{G})^{L^{+}G}$ is equivalent to the category of vector spaces, so the Hecke action carries no information. Therefore the strategy of [GR24a] does not work.

But there is a tool that still works as expected in the quantum setting and provides finer information than Hecke action: Whittaker coefficients. Thus instead, we are going to use this tool to construct ${\mathbb{L}}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{Betti}}$ . We also embed our construction of ${\mathbb{L}}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{Betti}}$ into the formalism of 2-Fourier-Mukai transform of [GR24b]. Recall that this is an equivalence between sheaves of categories over the 2-stacks ${\operatorname{Ge}}_{Z_{G}}$ and ${\operatorname{Ge}}_{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}$ , which classify gerbes on $X$ with respect to $Z_{G}$ and $\pi_{1}(\check{G})$ .

In Section 7 we upgrade the categories ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})$ and $\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})$ to sheave of categories over and ${\operatorname{Ge}}_{Z_{G}}$ and ${\operatorname{Ge}}_{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}$ respectively, and the assertion is that the resulting two sheaves of categories map to one another under the 2-categorical Fourier-Mukai transform. This implies that ${\mathbb{L}}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{Betti}}$ intertwines convolution action of ${\operatorname{Shv}}(\Bun_{Z_{G}})$ on ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})$ with the action of $\QCoh({\operatorname{Ge}}_{\pi_{1}(\check{G})})$ on $\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})$ via the 1-categorical Fourier-Mukai equivalence

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}(\Bun_{Z_{G}})\cong\QCoh({\operatorname{Ge}}_{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}). $$

As an application, using this we generalize the result of [Bog25] from the case of adjoint group $G$ to the case of arbitrary $G$ .

### 1.3. Outline of the proof.

Recall that there are several properties of ${\mathbb{L}}^{\operatorname{Betti}}$ that fix the functor uniquely. Among these is the condition that “the first Fourier coefficient” functor on $\D({\Bun_{G}})$ correspond to the functor $\Gamma({\operatorname{LS}}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{Betti}},-)$ .

The quantum version of this compatibility can be expressed as the commutativity of the diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G)_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma^{{\operatorname{lax}}}({\operatorname{Ran}},\Rep_{q}(\check{G}))} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G}).} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{FLE}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathbb{L}}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{Betti}}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{coeff}}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma_{q}} $$

Here the top arrow is the Fundamental Local Equivalence (see Subsection 6.2) between the category of Whittaker ind-constructible sheaves on the Beilinson-Drinfeld Grassmannian and (the appropriate ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ -version of) the category of representations of the quantum group, ${\operatorname{coeff}}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}$ is the Whittaker coefficient functor defined in Subsection 2.1, and $\Gamma_{q}$ is the functor discussed in Corollary 5.4. Let us say more about the definition of $\Gamma^{{\operatorname{lax}}}({\operatorname{Ran}},\Rep_{q}(\check{G}))$ . As was mentioned, from the category $\Rep_{q}(\check{G})$ we can form a cosheaf of categories $\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}$ on ${\operatorname{Ran}}(X)$ . Then $\Gamma^{{\operatorname{lax}}}({\operatorname{Ran}},\Rep_{q}(\check{G}))$ is the category of lax global sections of this cosheaf. Informally, this means that for every $x\in X$ we need to give an element $V_{x}\in\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{x}$ , and for every specialization $x\rightsquigarrow y$ we need to give a map $m_{x\rightsquigarrow y}(V_{x})\rightarrow V_{y}$ , where $m_{x\rightsquigarrow y}:\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{x}\rightarrow\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{y}$ is the corresponding specialization map.

So to give the construction of ${\mathbb{L}}_{\kappa}^{\operatorname{Betti}}$ the first thing we do is, parallel to the de Rham case ([Gai14, Proposition 4.3.4]), prove that $\Gamma_{q}$ is fully faithful (Corollary 5.4). Then we formulate the property that distinguished $\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})$ inside $\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}$ . Informally, the property says that the collection

$$ \{V_{x}\}_{x\in X}\in\Gamma^{{\operatorname{lax}}}({\operatorname{Ran}},\Rep_{q}(\check{G})) $$

lies in $\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})$ if and only if for every specialization $x\rightsquigarrow y$ the natural map

$$ V_{x}\rightarrow m_{x\rightsquigarrow y}^{R}(V_{y}) $$

is an isomorphism.

Let us explain how to check this property on $X^{2}$ . Let us also assume, for simplicity, that the tangent bundle to $X$ is trivial. It suffices to show that for every ${\mathcal{G}}\in\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta}}$ , and

$$ {\mathcal{F}}\in{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa\boxtimes{\operatorname{triv}},\Nilp\times T^{*}X^{2}}(\Bun_{G}\times X^{2}) $$

we have

$$ \langle{\operatorname{coeff}}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}({\mathcal{F}})_{X_{\Delta}},m_{\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta}}}({\mathcal{G}})\rangle\cong\langle{\operatorname{coeff}}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}({\mathcal{F}})_{X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta}},{\mathcal{G}}\rangle, $$

where $\langle-,-\rangle$ are the duality pairings, and

$$ m_{\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta}}}:\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta}}\rightarrow\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{X_{\Delta}} $$

is the map

$$ \LocSys(X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta})\otimes\Rep_{q}(\check{G})^{\otimes 2}\rightarrow\LocSys(X_{\Delta})\otimes\Rep_{q}(\check{G}) $$

coming from the ${\mathbb{E}}_{2}$ -structure on $\Rep_{q}(\check{G})$ and encoding all $m_{x\rightsquigarrow y}$ .

To show (1.2), we consider the functors

$$ {\operatorname{Poinc}}_{*,{\operatorname{co}}}:=({\operatorname{coeff}}^{{\operatorname{loc}}})^{\vee}:\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta}}\rightarrow{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa\boxtimes{\operatorname{triv}},\Nilp\times T^{*}(X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta})}(\Bun_{G}\times(X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta})) $$

and

$$ F:{\operatorname{Shv}}_{{\operatorname{triv}}\boxtimes\kappa,T^{*}(X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta})\times\Nilp}((X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta})\times\Bun_{G})\rightarrow{\operatorname{Shv}}(X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta}) $$

defined as

$$ {\mathcal{F}}^{\prime}\rightarrow p_{{X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta}}_{{\operatorname{disj}}},*}({\mathcal{F}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle!}}{{\otimes}}{\mathcal{F}}^{\prime}). $$

We show that they have the property of being defined and codefined by a kernel, a notion introduced in [AGK+22a]. In particular, this means that both (1.3) and (1.4) commute with $m_{\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{X^{2}\setminus X_{\Delta}}}$ , which gives the desired equivalence (1.2).

### 1.4. Notations and conventions.

#### 1.4.1. Categories.

We use the formalism of $\infty$ -categories developed in [Lur09], [Lur17], and theory of DG categories as understood in [GR17]. By a DG category we mean $k$ -linear stable $\infty$ -category. We let $\DGCat$ be the category of presentable DG categories with continuous functors with monoidal structure given by the Lurie tensor product $\otimes$ .

#### 1.4.2. Lie theory.

Throughout the paper $G$ will stand for a reductive group over $k$ of adjoint type. We choose Borel subgroup $B\subset G$ , the opposite Borel $B^{-}\subset G$ and the Cartan subgroup $T=B\cap B^{-}$ . Let $N$ ( $N^{-}$ ) be the unipotent radical of $B$ ( $B^{-}$ ). Let $\Lambda$ ( $\check{\Lambda}$ ) denote the lattice of weights (coweights) of $G$ . Let $\Lambda^{+}$ ( $\check{\Lambda}^{+}$ ) denote the subset of dominant weights (coweights). Let ${\mathcal{I}}$ denote the set of nodes for the Dynkin diagram of $G$ . For $i\in{\mathcal{I}}$ , we let $\alpha_{i}$ ( $\check{\alpha}_{i}$ ) denote the corresponding simple root (coroot). Let $2\rho$ denote the sum of simple roots and $2\check{\rho}$ the sum of simple coroots. Let $\check{G}$ be the Langlands dual group over $k$ for $G$ . We denote by $LG$ ( $L^{+}G$ ) the loop (arc) group of $G$ .

Let $\mathfrak{g}_{\irr}\subset\mathfrak{g}$ denote the reduced closed subscheme of irregular elements. We let ${\mathcal{N}}\subset\mathfrak{g}$ denote the nilpotent cone. We let ${\mathcal{N}}^{\irr}:={\mathcal{N}}\cap\mathfrak{g}_{\irr}$ denote the subscheme of irregular nilpotent elements. We let ${\mathcal{N}}^{\reg}\subset{\mathcal{N}}$ denote the open complement to ${\mathcal{N}}^{\irr}$ , which parametrizes of regular nilpotent elements.

#### 1.4.3. Levels.

A level $\kappa$ for $G$ is a $G$ -invariant symmetric bilinear form

$$ \kappa:\Sym^{2}(\mathfrak{g})\rightarrow{\mathbb{C}}. $$

Denote by $\kappa_{\mathfrak{g},\operatorname{crit}}$ the critical level, i.e. $-\frac{1}{2}$ times the Killing form. Throughout the paper we will assume that the level $\kappa$ is non-degenerate, i.e. that $\kappa-\kappa_{\mathfrak{g},\operatorname{crit}}$ is nondegenerate as a bilinear form. The dual level $\check{\kappa}$ on $\check{G}$ for $\kappa$ is the unique nondegenerate level such that the restriction of $\check{\kappa}-\kappa_{\check{\mathfrak{g}},\operatorname{crit}}$ to $\mathfrak{t}^{*}$ and the restriction of $\kappa-\kappa_{\mathfrak{g},\operatorname{crit}}$ to $\mathfrak{t}$ are dual symmetric bilinear forms.

Suppose $G$ is simple. A level $\kappa$ is rational if $\kappa$ is a rational multiple of the Killing form and irrational otherwise. A level $\kappa$ is positive if $\kappa-\kappa_{\mathfrak{g},\operatorname{crit}}$ is a positive rational multiple of the Killing form. A level is negative if it is not positive or critical. For general reductive $G$ , we say a level $\kappa$ is rational, irrational, positive, or negative if its restrictions to each simple factor are so.

Let $q$ be the quantum parameter associated to $\kappa$ . Namely,

$$ q=\exp(2\pi iq_{\kappa}), $$

where $q_{\kappa}$ is the quadratic form $\Lambda\rightarrow k$ such that the associated bilinear form is $\kappa$ .

#### 1.4.4. (Twisted) sheaves.

We will work in one of the following sheaf-theoretic contexts:

- • $\D(-)$ denotes the category of D-modules;

- • ${\operatorname{Shv}}(-)$ denoted the category of weakly constructible Betti sheaves (as in [MS22]).

For a level $\kappa$ , let $\D_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})$ be the category of $\kappa$ -twisted D-modules as in [ABC+24a, Section 10.1].

By [GL18, Proposition 3.1.9] from a fixed level $\kappa$ one gets a factorization gerbe ${\mathcal{G}}_{G}$ on $\Gra_{G}$ , which descends to $\Bun_{G}$ . We let ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})$ be the category of sheaves on $\Bun_{G}$ twisted by ${\mathcal{G}}_{G}$ .

#### Remark 1.4.5.

Note that by [AGK+22b, G.2] all Betti sheaves on $\Bun_{G}$ with microsupport in $\Nilp\subset T^{*}\Bun_{G}$ are weakly constructible.

#### 1.4.6. Ran space(s) and factorization.

In the geometric situation, the notation ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ for the Ran space is borrowed from [ABC+24a]. We refer to loc.cit. for generalities on Ran spaces and factorization.

The topological Ran space ${\operatorname{Ran}}(M)$ is as in [Lur17, Chapter 5].

## 2. Generalities.

### 2.1. Whittaker coefficients and Poincare functors.

#### 2.1.1.

Recall the Kirillov model of the Whittaker category from [Gai20, Section 1.6]. Namely, consider a category $\mathbf{C}$ with the action of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes{\mathbb{G}}_{a}$ . Let $\operatorname{Kir}(\mathbf{C})$ denote the quotient $\mathbf{C}^{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}/\mathbf{C}^{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes{\mathbb{G}}_{a}}$ , where we use the forgetful functor

$$ \mathbf{C}^{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes{\mathbb{G}}_{a}}\hookrightarrow\mathbf{C}^{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}. $$

The natural map $p:\mathbf{C}^{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}\rightarrow\operatorname{Kir}(\mathbf{C})$ admits a fully faithful right adjoint denoted by $p^{R}$ and a fully fithful left adjoint denoted by $p^{L}$ .

Consider $LN$ and its non-degenerate character $\chi$ , and $\mathbf{C}={\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X}),x})^{\ker(\chi)}$ . Then $\mathbf{C}$ admits an action of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ via $\check{\rho}$ , and we get

#### Notation 2.1.2.

${\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa,x}(G):=\operatorname{Kir}({\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X}),x})).$

The similar construction works in the setting of Beilinson-Drinfeld affine Grassmannian:

#### Notation 2.1.3.

${\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G):=\operatorname{Kir}({\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})).$

#### 2.1.4.

The Whittaker category admits a global model. Namely, for ${\mathcal{Z}}\rightarrow{\operatorname{Ran}}$ let ${\overline{\Bun}_{N,\rho(\omega_{X}),{\mathcal{Z}}}}$ be the stack introduced in [CCF+24, Section 10.2.1]. Denote by $\bar{p}_{{\mathcal{Z}}}$ the projection

$$ {\overline{\Bun}_{N,\rho(\omega_{X}),{\mathcal{Z}}}}\rightarrow\Bun_{G}\times{\mathcal{Z}}. $$

Denote by ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}({\overline{\Bun}_{N,\rho(\omega_{X}),{\mathcal{Z}}}})$ the corresponding category of twisted sheaves, by means of the pullback of the gerbe corresponding to $\kappa$ . Following [Gai20, Section 4.7] we can define a full Kirillov model subcategory

$$ {\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G)^{\operatorname{glob}}\subset{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}({\overline{\Bun}_{N,\rho(\omega_{X}),{\mathcal{Z}}}})^{\mathbb{G}_{m}}. $$

We have a naturally defined map

$$ \pi_{{\mathcal{Z}}}:\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X}),{\mathcal{Z}}}\rightarrow{\overline{\Bun}_{N,\rho(\omega_{X}),{\mathcal{Z}}}}. $$

#### Theorem 2.1.5.

[Gai20, Theorem 5.1.4] The functor $(\pi_{{\mathcal{Z}}})^{*}$ induces an equivalence

$$ {\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G)^{\operatorname{glob}}\xrightarrow{\cong}{\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G). $$

We refer to [ABC+24a, Section 9] and [CCF+24, Section 10.2] for more details.

#### Remark 2.1.6.

Note that the pairing $\Gamma_{!}(-\overset{*}{\otimes}-)$ induced the duality between between ${\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G)$ and ${\operatorname{Whit}}_{-\kappa}(G)$ .

#### 2.1.7.

We define the functor

$$ {\operatorname{coeff}}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}:{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})\rightarrow{\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G) $$

as ${\operatorname{coeff}}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}:={\operatorname{Av}}_{*,\chi}\circ\pi^{!}$ . Alternatively, the functor ${\operatorname{coeff}}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}$ can also be described as the composition

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})\xrightarrow{!-\text{pull}}{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}({\overline{\Bun}_{N,\rho(\omega_{X}),{\mathcal{Z}}}})^{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}\xrightarrow{{\operatorname{Av}}_{*}}{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}({\overline{\Bun}_{N,\rho(\omega_{X}),{\mathcal{Z}}}}/\ker(\chi))^{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}\xrightarrow{p}{\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G) $$

We define the functor

$$ {\operatorname{coeff}}_{!}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}:{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})\rightarrow{\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G) $$

as the composition

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})\xrightarrow{*-\text{pull}}{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}({\overline{\Bun}_{N,\rho(\omega_{X}),{\mathcal{Z}}}})^{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}\xrightarrow{{\operatorname{Av}}_{!}}{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}({\overline{\Bun}_{N,\rho(\omega_{X}),{\mathcal{Z}}}}/\ker(\chi))^{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}\xrightarrow{p}{\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G). $$

## 3. Miraculous duality for Betti sheaves.

In this section we develop the miraculous duality functor in the context of Betti sheaves and prove that it is an equivalence. The main resultion of this section, Theorem 3.1.8, will be used in Section 4.3.

### 3.1. The unit.

Let us introduce the following category (defined in the de Rham context in [DG15]):

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}}:=\colim_{U\subset\Bun_{G}}{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(U), $$

where the colimit is taken over the poset of open substacks such that the intersection with every connected component of $\Bun_{G}$ is quasi-compact, and the transition functors are given by $j_{*}$ .

#### Remark 3.1.1.

There is a natural functor

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}}\rightarrow{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G}). $$

However, it fails to be an equivalence.

#### 3.1.2.

Let ${\mathcal{Y}}$ be a QCA stack (see [DG15] for the terminology). Let $i:{\mathcal{Z}}\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{Y}}$ be a closed substack, let $j:U\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{Y}}$ be the complement open.

Following [DG15, Definition 2.1.6], we introduce:

#### Definition 3.1.3.

The substack $i:{\mathcal{Z}}\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{Y}}$ is called truncative (resp. $j:U\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{Y}}$ is called co-truncative) if $i^{!}$ is defined on all ${\operatorname{Shv}}({\mathcal{Y}})$ and admits a continuous right adjoint. Equivalently, if $j_{*}$ is defined on all ${\operatorname{Shv}}(U)$ and admits a continuous right adjoint.

#### Definition 3.1.4.

A locally QCA stack ${\mathcal{Y}}$ is called truncatable if it can be covered by open substacks which are co-truncative.

#### Proposition 3.1.5.

The stack $\Bun_{G}$ is truncatable.

#### Proof.

Follows the proof of [DG15, Theorem 4.1.12] by adapting the proofs of Propositions 2.5.2 and 2.3.4 to the Betti context. ∎

#### Corollary 3.1.6.

We have

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})\cong\lim_{U\subset\Bun_{G}}{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(U), $$

where the limit is taken over the poset of co-truncative open quasi-compact substacks of $\Bun_{G}$ ;

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}}\cong\colim_{U\subset\Bun_{G}}{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(U), $$

where the limit is taken over the poset of co-truncative open quasi-compact substacks of $\Bun_{G}$ .

#### Construction 3.1.7.

By Corollary 3.1.6, the category ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{-\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}}$ is dualizable. Therefore, the category

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})\otimes{\operatorname{Shv}}_{-\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}} $$

can be identified with

$$ \lim_{U\subset\Bun_{G}}({\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(U)\otimes{\operatorname{Shv}}_{-\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}}). $$

Let us define an object

$$ \Delta_{*,co}(\omega)\in{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})\otimes{\operatorname{Shv}}_{-\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}}. $$

As a compatible system of objects in the formula (3.4), the object $\Delta_{*,co}(\omega)$ is

$$ j_{*,{\operatorname{co}}}\circ\Delta_{*}(\omega_{U})\in{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(U)\otimes{\operatorname{Shv}}_{-\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}}. $$

Here $\omega$ is the dualizing object.

The object $\Delta_{*,co}(\omega)$ defines a functor

$$ \Vect\rightarrow{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})\otimes{\operatorname{Shv}}_{-\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}}, $$

and by duaity between ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})$ and ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{-\kappa}(\Bun_{G})$ described in Remark 2.1.9 this gives a functor

$$ \psid^{\mir}:{\operatorname{Shv}}_{-\kappa}(\Bun_{G})\rightarrow{\operatorname{Shv}}_{-\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}}. $$

The goal of this section is to prove the following Betti analog of the Miraculous duality for $\Bun_{G}$ :

#### Theorem 3.1.8.

The object

$$ \Delta_{*,co}(\omega)\in{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})\otimes{\operatorname{Shv}}_{-\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}} $$

defines a duality between ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})$ and ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{-\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}}$ . In other words, the functor $\psid^{\mir}$ is an equivalence.

Define

$$ \Eis_{{\operatorname{co}},*}^{\mu}:{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{M}^{\mu})_{{\operatorname{co}}}\rightarrow{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})_{{\operatorname{co}}} $$

as a compatible system of $\Eis_{*}^{\mu}$ functors on open co-truncative substacks. Define

$$ \Eis_{{\operatorname{co}},*}:=\bigoplus\Eis_{{\operatorname{co}},*}^{\mu}. $$

#### Proposition 3.1.9.

The functor $\Eis_{{\operatorname{co}},*}$ admits a continuous right adjoint $\Eis_{{\operatorname{co}},*}^{R}$ .

#### Proof.

By [Gai16, Proposition 2.4.3], on every open co-truncative substack the functor $\Eis_{*}$ admits a finite filtration by functors $\Eis_{!}\circ H^{\alpha}(-)$ , where $H^{\alpha}(-):=\overset{\leftarrow}{h}_{!}(\overset{\rightarrow}{h^{*}}(-)\overset{*}{\otimes}K^{\alpha})$ . We note that $\Eis_{!}$ admits a continuous right adjoint, and $H^{\alpha}$ does as well since $K^{\alpha}$ is ULA relative to $\overset{\rightarrow}{h}$ . Therefore on every open co-truncative substack the functor $\Eis_{*}$ admits a continuous right adjoint, and thus $\Eis_{{\operatorname{co}},*}$ admits a continuous right adjoint as well. ∎

### 5.1. Constructible cosheaves of categories.

#### Notation 5.1.1.

[Lej21, Definition 2.12] Denote by ${\operatorname{StratTop}}$ the category of conically stratified $D_{\omega}$ topological spaces.

#### Notation 5.1.2.

[Lej21, Definition 1.22] For a topological space $X$ let ${\operatorname{Shv}}(X,\mathbf{D})$ (resp. ${\operatorname{cShv}}(X,\mathbf{D})$ ) be the category of $\mathbf{D}$ -valued hyper(co)complete (co)sheaves on $X$ . For

Informally, a cosheaf ${\mathcal{F}}\in{\operatorname{cShv}}(X,\mathbf{D})$ gives the data of an element ${\mathcal{F}}_{x}\in\mathbf{D}$ for every $x\in X$ , and for every specialization map $x\rightsquigarrow y$ the data of a map ${\mathcal{F}}_{x}\rightarrow{\mathcal{F}}_{y}$ .

where $f_{*}$ stands for the cosheaf pushforward, and $f^{*}$ stands for cosheaf hyperpullback ([Lej21, Definition 1.5, Corollary 2.18]).

#### Remark 5.1.4.

The category ${\operatorname{cShv}}(X,\mathbf{D})$ has a canonical symmetric monoidal structure. The subcategory ${\operatorname{cShv}}_{A}(X,\mathbf{D})$ is stable under this tensor product.

Let ${\operatorname{Exit}}_{A}$ be the exit-path category of [Lur17, Appendix A.6]. Let ${\operatorname{Enter}}_{A}:={\operatorname{Exit}}_{A}^{\op}$ .

#### Remark 5.1.5.

[Lej21, Corollary 3.12] For $X\rightarrow A\in{\operatorname{StratTop}}$ we have

$$ \operatorname{Fun}({\operatorname{Exit}}_{A},\mathbf{D})\cong{\operatorname{Shv}}_{A}(X,\mathbf{D}), $$

### 6.1. Construction of the local Whittaker coefficients functor.

The goal of this section is to construct the functor

$$ {\operatorname{coeff}}_{!}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}({\mathcal{F}})_{X(a)}\in{\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G)_{X(a)}\subset{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X}),{X(a)}}) $$

is ULA with respect to the projection $p_{a}:\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X}),{X(a)}}\rightarrow X(a).$ Denote by

$$ \langle-,-\rangle:{\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G)_{X(a)}\otimes_{{\operatorname{Shv}}(X(a))}({\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G)_{X(a)})^{\vee}\rightarrow{\operatorname{Shv}}(X(a)) $$

the natural pairing induced from the pairing

$$ ({\mathcal{F}},{\mathcal{G}})\mapsto p_{a,*}({\mathcal{F}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle!}}{{\otimes}}{\mathcal{G}}). $$

Fix ${\mathcal{G}}\in{\operatorname{Whit}}(G)_{X(a)}$ ULA with respect to $p_{a}$ . Note that by duality

$$ \langle{\operatorname{coeff}}_{!}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}({\mathcal{F}})_{X(a)},{\mathcal{G}}\rangle\cong\langle{\mathcal{F}},{\operatorname{Poinc}}_{!}({\mathcal{G}})\rangle:=\pi_{X(a),!}({\mathcal{F}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle*}}{{\otimes}}{\operatorname{Poinc}}_{!}({\mathcal{G}})), $$

where $\pi_{X(a)}:\Bun_{G}\times X(a)\rightarrow X(a)$ is the projection. By Corollary 4.2.7 and [AGK+22a, Corollary B.10.7] the sheaf ${\operatorname{Poinc}}_{!}({\mathcal{G}})$ is ULA with respect to $\pi_{X(a)}$ . But since ${\mathcal{F}}$ has nilpotent singular support, by Theorem 4.3.1 and [AGK+22a, Corollary B.10.7] we get that

$$ \pi_{X(a),!}({\mathcal{F}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle*}}{{\otimes}}{\operatorname{Poinc}}_{!}({\mathcal{G}})) $$

is ULA with respect to $\Id$ , which finishes the proof. ∎

### 6.2. Quantum Fundamental Local Equivalence.

One of the key ingredients in the construction of the quantum Langlands functor will be the quantum version of the Fundamental Local Equivalence ([ABC+24a, Theorem 6.1.4]). A recent result of Gaitsgory and Hayash provides the construction of the functor in our setting:

#### Theorem 6.2.1.

[GH25] There exists a canonical functor

$$ \operatorname{FLE}:{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}\rightarrow\Gamma^{{\operatorname{lax}}}({\operatorname{Ran}},\Rep_{q}(\check{G})). $$

We will need a stronger expected result:

#### Conjecture 3 (Gaitsgory, Lurie).

The functor (6.2) is an equivalence.

#### Remark 6.2.2.

Let us describe explicitly what Conjecture 3 says. Recall from [CF21, Lemma 6.2.1] (and Verdier duality [Lur17, Theorem 5.5.5.1]) that ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}(\Gra_{G})$ is equivalent to the lax limit of ${\operatorname{LS}}_{\kappa}(\Gra_{G,X(a)})$ for $a\in A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}$ , where the connecting functors are $j_{b}^{!}j_{a,!}$ for $a\rightarrow b\in A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}$ . Moreover, the functors $j_{b}^{!}j_{a,!}$ send the subcategory

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}(\Gra_{G})^{LN,\chi}_{X(a)} $$

to the subcategory

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}(\Gra_{G})^{LN,\chi}_{X(b)}. $$

In other words, the category ${\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}$ can also we described as a lax limit with connecting functors $j_{b}^{!}j_{a,!}$ .

On the other hand, recall the description of $\Gamma^{{\operatorname{lax}}}({\operatorname{Ran}},\Rep_{q}(\check{G}))$ from Corollary 5.3.5. In [GH25], the authors prove that for every $a\in A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}$ the functor

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}(\Gra_{G})^{LN,\chi}_{X(a)}\rightarrow\Gamma(X(a),\Rep_{q}(\check{G})) $$

is an equivalence. Thus, Conjecture 3 amounts to show that the map

$$ \operatorname{FLE}(j_{b}^{!}j_{a,!})\rightarrow\phi_{2,\Rep_{q}(\check{G})}\circ\phi_{1,\Rep_{q}(\check{G})} $$

is an equivalence.

#### Remark 6.2.3.

The construction of the functor (6.2) from [GH25] (and the proof that the functor is equivalence at a point) follows the strategy of [GL19]. Namely, it reduces to the know case of $G=T$ as follows. Gaitsgory and Hayash prove that

$$ \Gamma^{{\operatorname{lax}}}({\operatorname{Ran}},\Rep_{q}(\check{G}))\cong\Gamma^{{\operatorname{lax}}}({\operatorname{Ran}},\Omega_{q}\operatorname{-mod}^{{\mathcal{E}}_{2}}(A_{q}\Mmod(\Rep_{\check{q}}(T)))), $$

where the factorization algebra $\Omega_{q}$ is as in [GL19], and $A_{q}:={\mathcal{O}}_{N_{H}}$ is an algebra in

$$ \Rep(T_{H})\subset\Rep_{\check{q}}(\check{T}). $$

Similarly, they prove that

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}(\Gra_{G})^{LN,\chi}\cong\Omega^{{\operatorname{Whit}}}\operatorname{-FactMod}(A^{{\operatorname{Whit}}}\Mmod({\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}(\Gra_{T}))). $$

Finally, they check that the factorization algebras $\Omega_{q}$ and $\Omega^{{\operatorname{Whit}}}$ , and $A_{q}$ and $A^{{\operatorname{Whit}}}$ correspond to one another under the toric FLE.

### 6.3. Construction of the quantum Langlands functor in the Betti context.

Recall that in section 6.1 we constructed

$$ {\operatorname{coeff}}_{!}^{\operatorname{loc}}:{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})\rightarrow{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}. $$

We are now ready to prove our main result.

#### Theorem 6.3.1.

The composition

$$ \operatorname{FLE}\circ{\operatorname{coeff}}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}:{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})\rightarrow{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}\cong\Gamma^{{\operatorname{lax}}}({\operatorname{Ran}},\Rep_{q}(\check{G})) $$

factors through $\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})$ .

#### Notation 6.3.2.

Denote the resulting functor

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})\rightarrow\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G}) $$

by ${\mathbb{L}}$ .

The result will follows from Propoosition 5.4.6 and the following claim:

#### Proposition 6.3.3.

In the notation of Construction 5.3.3, for every $\alpha:I\twoheadrightarrow J$ , ${\mathcal{G}}\in{\operatorname{Whit}}_{-\kappa,X^{I}}$ , and ${\mathcal{F}}\in{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa\boxtimes{\operatorname{triv}},\Nilp\times T^{*}X^{I}}(\Bun_{G}\times X^{I})$ we have

$$ \langle{\operatorname{coeff}}_{!}({\mathcal{F}})_{X^{J}_{{\operatorname{disj}}}},\phi_{2,A^{\vee}}\circ\phi_{1,A^{\vee}}({\mathcal{G}})\rangle\cong\langle\phi_{1}({\operatorname{coeff}}_{!}({\mathcal{F}})_{X^{I}_{{\operatorname{disj}}}}),\phi_{1,A^{\vee}}({\mathcal{G}})\rangle $$

#### Proof.

Rewrite by duality

$$ \langle{\operatorname{coeff}}_{!}({\mathcal{F}})_{X^{J}_{{\operatorname{disj}}}},\phi_{2,A^{\vee}}\circ\phi_{1,A^{\vee}}({\mathcal{G}})\rangle\cong\langle({\mathcal{F}})_{X^{J}_{{\operatorname{disj}}}},{\operatorname{Poinc}}_{!}\circ\phi_{2,A^{\vee}}\circ\phi_{1,A^{\vee}}({\mathcal{G}})\rangle. $$

By Corollary 4.2.7 we can rewrite (6.8) as

$$ \langle({\mathcal{F}})_{X^{J}_{{\operatorname{disj}}}},\phi_{2,A^{\vee}}\circ\phi_{1,A^{\vee}}\circ{\operatorname{Poinc}}_{!}({\mathcal{G}})\rangle, $$

and by Theorem 4.3.1 we further rewrite it as

$$ \Gamma_{c}\circ\phi_{2,\Vect}\circ\phi_{1,\Vect}\langle({\mathcal{F}})_{X^{I}_{{\operatorname{disj}}}},{\operatorname{Poinc}}_{!}({\mathcal{G}})\rangle_{X^{I}}, $$

where $\langle-,-\rangle_{X^{I}}:=\pi_{X^{I},!}(-\stackrel{{\scriptstyle*}}{{\otimes}}-).$ However, (6.9) agrees with $\langle\phi_{1}({\operatorname{coeff}}_{!}({\mathcal{F}})_{X^{I}_{{\operatorname{disj}}}}),\phi_{1,A^{\vee}}({\mathcal{G}})\rangle.$ ∎

## 7. 2-Fourier-Mukai transform and the quantum Langlands functor.

### 7.1. Sheaves associated with automorphic and spectral categories.

Let $G$ be a semisimple group. Consider categories

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})\quad\text{and}\quad\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G}). $$

We will now upgrade them to the elements

$$ \underline{{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})}\in\operatorname{ShvCat}({\operatorname{Ge}}_{Z_{G}}(X))\quad\text{and}\quad\underline{\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})}\in\operatorname{ShvCat}({\operatorname{Ge}}_{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}(X)). $$

#### 7.1.1.

The short exact sequence of groups

$$ 1\rightarrow Z_{G}\rightarrow G\rightarrow G_{\ad}\rightarrow 1 $$

induces a map

$$ \Bun_{G_{\ad}}\rightarrow{\operatorname{Ge}}_{Z_{G}}(X). $$

Since ${\operatorname{Ge}}_{Z_{G}}(X)$ is discrete, the map (7.4) induces on ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{{}^{\ad}})$ the structure of a sheaf of categories over ${\operatorname{Ge}}_{Z_{G}}(X)$ denoted by $\underline{{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})}$ .

#### 7.1.2.

Let us first upgrade the category $\Rep_{q}(\check{G})$ to

$$ \underline{\Rep_{q}(\check{G})}\in\operatorname{ShvCat}(B^{2}{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}). $$

Note that since $B^{2}\pi_{1}(\check{G})$ has only one equivalence class of points we have

$$ \operatorname{ShvCat}(B^{2}{\pi_{1}(\check{G})})\cong\QCoh(B{\pi_{1}(\check{G}))}_{\operatorname{conv}}\Mmod\cong\Rep(\pi_{1}(\check{G}))_{\operatorname{conv}}\Mmod. $$

Here the first equivalence is given by the fiber at the trivial element of $B^{2}{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}$ . Further, Fourier-Mukai transform gives

$$ \Rep(\pi_{1}(\check{G}))_{\operatorname{conv}}\Mmod\cong\QCoh(Z_{G})\Mmod\cong\operatorname{ShvCat}(Z_{G}). $$

Moreover, we have $Z_{G}\cong\pi_{1}(\check{G})^{\vee},$ so

$$ \operatorname{ShvCat}(Z_{G})\cong\operatorname{ShvCat}(\pi_{1}(\check{G})^{\vee}). $$

Let us now define an element in $\operatorname{ShvCat}(\pi_{1}(\check{G})^{\vee})$ corresponding to

$$ \underline{\Rep_{q}(\check{G})}\in\operatorname{ShvCat}(B^{2}{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}). $$

Note that $\pi_{1}(\check{G})\subseteq Z_{\check{G}^{{\operatorname{sc}}}}$ , and thus

$$ \operatorname{char}(Z_{\check{G}^{{\operatorname{sc}}}})\twoheadrightarrow\pi_{1}(\check{G})^{\vee}. $$

Then consider the category $\Rep_{q}(\check{G}^{\operatorname{sc}})$ . For every $V\in\Rep_{q}(\check{G}^{\operatorname{sc}})$ we have a canonical decomposition

$$ V\cong\oplus_{\chi\in\pi_{1}(\check{G})^{\vee}}V_{\chi}, $$

which upgrades $\Rep_{q}(\check{G}^{\operatorname{sc}})$ to an element in $\operatorname{ShvCat}(\pi_{1}(\check{G})^{\vee})$ .

#### 7.1.3.

Now let us define

$$ \underline{\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})}\in\operatorname{ShvCat}({\operatorname{Ge}}_{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}(X)). $$

For every affine $S$ with a map

$$ s:S\rightarrow{\operatorname{Ge}}_{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}(X) $$

we set

$$ s^{*}(\underline{\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})}):=\int_{X}(\Rep_{q}(\check{G}^{{\operatorname{sc}}}))_{{\mathcal{H}}_{s}}, $$

where ${\mathcal{H}}_{s}$ is the corresponding analytic $\pi_{1}(\check{G})$ -gerbe and $(\Rep_{q}(\check{G}^{{\operatorname{sc}}}))_{{\mathcal{H}}_{s}}$ is the ${\mathcal{E}}_{X^{\operatorname{an}}}$ -category obtained by twisting $\Rep_{q}(\check{G}^{{\operatorname{sc}}})$ .

### 7.2. 2-Fourier-Mukai transform and ${\mathbb{L}}$ .

The goal of this section is to prove:

#### Theorem 7.2.1.

There exists a natural functor

$$ \underline{{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})}\rightarrow\operatorname{2-FM}(\underline{\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})})\in\operatorname{ShvCat}({\operatorname{Ge}}_{Z_{G}}(X)) $$

compatible with ${\mathbb{L}}$ .

#### Remark 7.2.2.

The statement of Theorem 7.2.1 is equivalent to saying that there exists a natural functor

$$ \operatorname{2-FM}(\underline{{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})})\rightarrow\underline{\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})}\in\operatorname{ShvCat}(\operatorname{Ge}_{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}(X)) $$

compatible with ${\mathbb{L}}$ .

Note that Fourier-Mukai equivalence induces

$$ \operatorname{FM}:{\operatorname{Shv}}(\Bun_{Z_{G}})\cong\QCoh({\operatorname{Ge}}_{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}(X)). $$

Taking the fiber of (7.7) at the trivial gerbe $\sigma_{0}\in{\operatorname{Ge}}_{Z_{G}}(X)$ we get

#### Corollary 7.2.3.

For ${\mathcal{F}}\in{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})$ and ${\mathcal{M}}\in{\operatorname{Shv}}(\Bun_{Z_{G}})$ we have

$$ {\mathbb{L}}({\mathcal{M}}\textasteriskcentered{}{\mathcal{F}})\cong\operatorname{FM}({\mathcal{M}})\ast{\mathbb{L}}({\mathcal{F}}). $$

#### Proof of Theorem 7.2.1.

Take $\phi\in\operatorname{Ge}_{Z_{G}}(X)$ . Let us construct

$$ (\underline{{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,\Nilp}(\Bun_{G})})_{\phi}\rightarrow\operatorname{2-FM}(\underline{\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})})_{\phi}\cong(\underline{\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})})_{{\mathcal{G}}_{\phi}}. $$

Here ${\mathcal{G}}_{\phi}$ is the gerbe on $\operatorname{Ge}_{\pi_{1}(\check{G})}(X)$ corresponding to $\phi$ , and the last equivalence follows as in [GR24b, (8.11)].

Choose a point $x\in X$ . We can choose a trivialization of $\phi$ on $X\setminus x$ , so we can assume that $\phi$ came from an object

$$ \phi\in\operatorname{Fib}(\operatorname{Ge}_{Z_{G}}(X)\rightarrow\operatorname{Ge}_{Z_{G}}(X\setminus x))\cong Z_{G}(-1). $$

We claim that the proof of Theorem 6.3.1 applies in the context of (7.9) as well. Let us derive the $\phi$ -analog of Conjecture 6.2. We replace ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ by its pointed version ${\operatorname{Ran}}_{x}$ , and work over $\underline{x}\in{\operatorname{Ran}}_{x}$ , i.e. $\underline{x}:=\underline{x_{1}}\sqcup{x}$ . Replace

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}_{\underline{x}}:={\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{\underline{x_{1}}}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}_{\underline{x_{1}}}\otimes{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{x}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi} $$

by

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{x}}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}_{\underline{x},\phi}:={\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{\underline{x_{1}}}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}_{\underline{x_{1}}}\otimes{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{x}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}_{\phi}, $$

where ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{x}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}_{\phi}$ comes from the decomposition coming from connected components of the affine Grassmannian:

$$ {\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{x}}(\Gra_{G_{\ad},\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}\cong\oplus_{\phi\in Z_{G}(-1)}{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{x}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}_{\phi}. $$

Let $\eta_{\phi}$ be the character of $\pi_{1}(\check{G})$ corresponding to $\phi$ . Replace the factorization cosheaf $\Rep_{q}(\check{G})$ on ${\operatorname{Ran}}_{x}$ with

$$ \Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{\underline{x}}:=\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{\underline{x_{1}}}\otimes\Rep_{q}(\check{G}) $$

by the factorization cosheaf $\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{\eta_{\phi}}$ on ${\operatorname{Ran}}_{x}$ with

$$ \Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{\eta_{\phi},\underline{x}}:=\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{\underline{x_{1}}}\otimes\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{x,\eta_{\phi}}, $$

where $\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{x,\eta_{\phi}}$ is the summand in the decomposition of the category $\Rep_{q}(\check{G}^{\operatorname{sc}})$ over $\pi_{1}(\check{G})^{\vee}$ given in 7.1.2. Then to construct

$$ \operatorname{FLE}_{\phi}:{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{x}}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}_{\phi}\rightarrow\Gamma^{{\operatorname{lax}}}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{x},\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{\eta_{\phi}}) $$

it suffices to show that subcategories ${\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{x}}(\Gra_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}_{\phi}$ and $\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{x,\eta_{\phi}}$ correspond to one another under the equivalence

$$ \operatorname{FLE}_{x}:{\operatorname{Shv}}_{\kappa,A_{x}}(\Gra_{G_{\ad},\rho(\omega_{X})})^{LN,\chi}\cong\Rep_{q}(\check{G}^{\operatorname{sc}}) $$

of [GH25]. However, by Remark 6.2.3 (and since the factorization algebras $\Omega$ and algebras $A$ were independent of the center of the group) the statement reduces to the case of tori, where it is evident.

Note that the $\phi$ -analog of ${\operatorname{coeff}}^{\operatorname{loc}}$ is constructed similarly, and it is also defined and codefined by a kernel. Finally, note that choosing a trivialization of $\phi$ away from x we get

$$ (\underline{\int_{X}\Rep_{q}(\check{G})})_{{\mathcal{G}}_{\phi}}\cong\Gamma({\operatorname{Ran}}_{x},\Rep_{q}(\check{G})_{\eta_{\phi}}). $$

∎

## 8. Application: non-vanishing of quantum Whittaker coefficients for semi-simple groups.

As an application of Theorem 7.2.1 we are able to relax the condition on the center of $G$ in the results of [Bog25]:

#### Theorem 8.0.1.

For any semi-simple reductive group $G$ , the functor

$$ {\operatorname{coeff}}^{{\operatorname{loc}}}:\D_{\kappa}(\Bun_{G})^{{\operatorname{Wh-temp}}}\rightarrow{\operatorname{Whit}}_{\kappa}(G) $$

is conservative.

#### Proof.

Follows from [Bog25, Theorem 6.1.1], [FR22, Proposition 2.5.4.1(4)] and Theorem 7.2.1. ∎
